post.caption:
Pluto never moved and never shrank. It stopped being a planet because a room of astronomers in Prague changed what the word means.

One science fact a day. Follow so you don't miss tomorrow's.

#pluto #planets #solarsystem #space #astronomy #science #eris #dwarfplanet #spacefacts #sciencefacts #didyouknow

subject_anchor: planets, moons, orbits, star charts and the night sky
style_lock: photorealistic studio product photograph of a real physical object on a clean seamless pure white #FFFFFF background, soft even studio light, accurate materials and weight, only a light contact shadow beneath the object, no environment and no gradient; composited with one small flat hand-drawn anime mascot character standing in the scene: a solid matte black bean-shaped body about one tenth of the frame height, two small white dot eyes, thin simple stick arms and legs, slightly irregular hand-drawn outline, calm deadpan expression with no mouth, no clothing; a few small colour accents only, blue or yellow tape, a small green or red dot; generous empty white space, vertical portrait composition

beats.text: Pluto never moved, never shrank, and still stopped being a planet.
beats.image_prompt: a small grey rock resting on a low white museum pedestal, the mascot straining with both thin arms to hold its metal name plaque on as the last screw drops out

beats.text: For seventy six years it was the ninth dot on every classroom poster.
beats.image_prompt: a paper chart of the planets pinned to a white wall, the mascot hanging off its bottom corner so its weight peels the smallest planet at the end of the row away from the sheet

beats.text: Then astronomers found Eris, further out than Pluto and slightly heavier.
beats.image_prompt: a small brass balance scale holding one round grey rock in each pan, the mascot standing on tiptoe on the higher pan trying to weigh its side back down

beats.text: So either we had a tenth planet, or the word planet meant nothing.
beats.image_prompt: a neat row of nine small planet models standing on a white shelf, the mascot shoving a tenth model with both arms trying to wedge it into the end of the full row

beats.text: It had never actually been defined.
beats.image_prompt: a heavy open dictionary lying flat, the mascot kneeling on the page and peering down into one completely blank entry space through a magnifying glass twice its size

beats.text: So in two thousand six, astronomers finally wrote the rules.
beats.image_prompt: a single sheet of white paper carrying three empty ruled boxes, the mascot dragging an oversized pencil across it with both arms to finish ruling the third line

beats.text: Orbit the Sun. Be round. Sweep your own lane clean.
beats.image_prompt: a curved chalk track drawn on a white surface, the mascot sweeping loose grey pebbles off the track with a real broom, one round planet model parked on the cleared stretch behind it

beats.text: Pluto passes the first two easily.
beats.image_prompt: a round grey rock held up against a circular drafting template, the mascot pressing the two together with both arms to check the curve matches

beats.text: But its orbit is crowded with thousands of icy chunks it never cleared.
beats.image_prompt: a curved track buried under a thick spill of small ice cubes, the mascot shoving a round grey rock along it and getting nowhere, cubes piling up ahead of the rock

beats.text: So a few hundred astronomers in a hall in Prague raised their hands.
beats.image_prompt: one wooden auditorium seat with a small folded paper ballot lying on it, the mascot standing on the seat cushion with one thin arm raised straight up

beats.text: Pluto did not change that day. Our definition did.
beats.image_prompt: an open notebook page with a handwritten word on it, the mascot gripping a large pink eraser with both arms and rubbing the word half away, a small grey rock sitting untouched beside the page

beats.text: And every planet still on that list is stranger than the one we removed.
beats.image_prompt: eight planet models stacked in a tall vertical line on a white surface, the mascot at the base shouldering one of them over so it tips onto its side
